title: The Chow test: did the coefficients change at a known date?
concepts: F statistic from residual sums of squares

explain.prompt: In 5–7 sentences: state the null hypothesis of the Chow test and how the F statistic is built; interpret the result at 2016-01-01 and at the two placebo dates; explain why the same test on log levels rejects even at a placebo date and why that result must be ignored; list the assumptions that guided your choice of regression.
rubric: H0: the regression coefficients (constant and slope) are the same before and after the known date; H1: at least one differs.
F = [(SSR_pooled − SSR_1 − SSR_2)/k] / [(SSR_1 + SSR_2)/(n − 2k)], k = 2: the improvement in fit from separate lines relative to the remaining noise, compared with an F(k, n − 2k) distribution.

Daily log returns at 2016-01-01: F ≈ 107, p ≈ 0 → the short-run relationship changed (pass-through ≈ 0.59 → 0.89). Placebos inside a regime: p ≈ 0.50 (2014) and ≈ 0.92 (2018) → no change, as expected.

On log levels the test rejects even at the 2018 placebo (F ≈ 67): the variables are I(1) and the residuals persistent, so the F distribution does not apply — the rejection is an artefact, like the spurious t-statistics of 4.6.
Assumptions: date known in advance; stationary variables; errors independent over time with the same variance in both sub-periods — daily log returns satisfy them far better than levels.
Chow says THAT the coefficients differ, not why: the economic explanation (end of the export ban, arbitrage opened) comes from the mechanism.
